authorization: Owner requests 3 problems in parallel, one per PDF volume, targeting six hours per problem, working in /Users/jinleic/repos/aifours.
scope_rules: No automatic revisit, refill, extra problem, paid-API fallback, model/config change, scheduler, commit, push, or external contact.
A special case, finite search range, or improved bound is partial progress, not resolution of a broader book question.
Sampling is not independent exhaustive verification. Numerical negativity is not a theorem without its analytic bridge. Solver UNKNOWN is not UNSAT.
Openness and novelty are dated search verdicts. Preprints and openai/math are claims until independently established.

problems.title_zh: 凯莱 (Cayley) 图和相关的问题
problems.question: Does every finite flag-transitive projective plane have to be Desarguesian? Equivalently, for n>8 with p=n^2+n+1 prime, show D={x in F_p*: x^(n+1)=1} is not a planar difference set.
problems.relation_to_book: The geometric nonexistence conjecture is explicitly stated in the article. Its literal diameter-two Cayley-graph assertion is inconsistent; disclose it rather than silently correcting it.
problems.baseline: Thas-Zagier, JEMS10(2008): no non-Desarguesian flag-transitive projective plane for order n<200000000000. No later range extension located in the dated screen.
problems.bounded_target: Try to extend the computed nonexistence range to at least n<2000000000000, with exact interval coverage, known-case controls, a survivor/elimination table, and independent checks. Any finite range is a sub-question only.
problems.angle: Harden the staged segmented prime-divisor sieve plus 128-bit Montgomery base-two test on n=8 mod24. Restrict sieve rejection to proper divisors q<p. Controls must reproduce the published exceptional list. Declare the imported Feit/congruence theorems.
problems.risk: High plausibility for a producing range extension is inference, not a promise of proof. Sampled Python pow cross-checks and hashes do not certify every tested n; report that limit explicitly. Do not attack the trivial false literal diameter claim. Probable-prime survivors remain unresolved, not eliminated.
review_requirements: Do not say the target is the book Cayley-graph form or follows from the book stated equivalence. Disclose both printed problems: reflection-generated dihedral Cayley graphs are bipartite with degree smaller than either part, so diameter two is impossible; and the unspecified reflection set breaks the printed equivalence (classical Singer difference sets give diameter-three graphs for Desarguesian planes). Credit the reduction to Kantor plus Thas-Zagier.

Declare every imported premise: Kantor 1987 (relies on the classification of finite simple groups), the Thas-Zagier special-prime reduction and base-two condition, Feit 8|n, and the derivation of n congruent to 2 modulo 3.
Before the main scan, add the proper-divisor guard q

Cross-checks at main-range modulus sizes must compare full 2^(n+1) mod p residues and actual sieve divisors, not only survivor flags. Any contiguous hash must include every n decision and residue. A uniform failing big-integer bug must not masquerade as no survivors.

A probable-prime test cannot eliminate a survivor. Each survivor needs an exact elimination reason, such as an explicit proper factor or a proved necessary-condition failure; otherwise list it as unresolved.
Cap the main production scan at about 2.5 hours. Report N only as the end of the last unbroken audited block.

Defensible success wording: Assuming the declared imported theorems, one production computation excluded all candidates for 200000000000<=n<N in the audited congruence class; independent arbitrary-precision checks covered only stated subsets. Therefore no non-Desarguesian flag-transitive plane of order less than N exists, conditional on those premises. Never say the extended range was independently certified, and keep the all-orders conjecture open.
problems.solved_means: A proof for every order n>8 that no non-Desarguesian finite flag-transitive projective plane exists (equivalently, no special prime p=n^2+n+1), or an explicit counterexample plane verified directly.
problems.partial_means: An exactly scoped verified result, such as a gap-free finite range 200000000000<=n<N with every survivor eliminated under declared imported premises, or a proved new necessary condition.

problems.title_zh: 弹性布尔函数的非线性度的紧上界
problems.question: Does a balanced Boolean function f:F_2^9 -> F_2 with nonlinearity at least242 exist? Equivalently, wt(f)=256 and max_a |sum_x (-1)^(f(x)+a dot x)|<=28.
problems.relation_to_book: The smallest odd n>=9 instance of the book's explicitly open balanced-nonlinearity and above-bent-concatenation construction question.
problems.baseline: Best located balanced9-variable nonlinearity is240. Kavut-Yucel have unbalanced242 functions with no zero Walsh coefficients. Two 2026-10-13 preprints still list balanced9-variable242 as open.
problems.bounded_target: Primary success: an explicit512-bit truth table verified balanced and nl>=242 by an independent full Walsh computation. Otherwise attempt precisely delimited local-neighborhood or small symmetry-class exclusions; those are sub-questions only.
problems.angle: Exact local balancing around the staged unbalanced242 seed tables; use z3 or cardinality SAT with independently reconstructed Walsh constraints. Concurrently try a seeded heuristic. Limit exact symmetry enumeration to feasible classes, after checking it is not already prior art.
problems.risk: Low probability of a positive242 witness in six hours. A timeout or heuristic non-find proves nothing. Two solvers sharing one encoding are not a model-independent certificate; unsupported UNSAT claims are not accepted. Do not assume the unrefereed claimed upper bound242 to validate a positive witness.
review_requirements: Positive success requires an explicit indexed 512-bit truth table, its bit order and SHA-256, weight 256 after any linear balancing step, and every Walsh coefficient magnitude at most 28. Verify independently using FWHT and direct character sums.
Search for max|W|<=28 with some W(a)=0; adding a linear function a.x then balances without changing nonlinearity.

A positive witness establishes existence only for n=9. Do not claim optimality, maximum balanced nonlinearity 242, or a general odd-n construction. The 2026 upper-bound claim is unrefereed and must not be used; nonlinearity 244 would contradict it and must be reported as such.
Local radii below the forced distance |W_g(0)|/2 are vacuous. Report this minimum next to each radius. The weight-242 seed with W(0)=28 needs r>=14.

Before enumeration, screen every symmetry class for an affine conjugate of the nine-cycle coordinate shift. Such classes are affine-equivalent to rotation-symmetric functions and already excluded at nonlinearity 242; e.g. multiplicative F_8* plus Frobenius is already settled.

A negative result needs the exact seed/radius or class definition, justified completeness, and independently audited question-to-encoding correspondence: planted solvable variants and random assignments checked against direct Walsh calculation. Several solvers on one CNF are one unchecked result. Timeout, UNKNOWN, and heuristic non-find prove no absence. An exact class maximum also needs an attaining witness.
problems.solved_means: An explicit balanced f:F_2^9->F_2 whose 512 Walsh coefficients all have magnitude at most 28, independently verified (settles existence at n=9 only), or a complete proof that none exists.
problems.partial_means: An exactly scoped verified result, such as non-vacuous seed-neighbourhood or symmetry-class exclusions with audited encodings, or an exact class maximum with an attaining witness.

problems.title_zh: 用统计物理学方法处理约束满足问题面临的五个挑战
problems.question: Challenge5: rigorously calculate improved upper bounds for SAT/UNSAT phase transitions in random k-SAT; focus on k=4 and5 within this visit.
problems.relation_to_book: The book explicitly requests certified bounds via interval arithmetic or other rigorous numerical methods. k=4,5 improvements would address part of that challenge, not solve all five challenges or determine exact thresholds.
problems.baseline: Opened Achlioptas-Peres table: upper bounds10.23(k=4),21.33(k=5),87.88(k=7). Recheck current literature. Vorobyev2610.10599 claims4.268 for k=3 only; it is an unrefereed method lead.
problems.bounded_target: Aim for certified rational a4<10.23 and a5<21.33 proving P[random distinct-variable k-SAT with floor(ak*n) clauses is satisfiable]->0. Probes suggest9.94 and21.125 but are not certificates. Improvements remain partial book-level progress.
problems.angle: Establish the general-k energetic interpolation inequality and its model transfer; then certify a rational multi-warning trial with rigorous truncation/error bounds and an independent checker, starting with k=4,5. Use k=3 reproduction and known satisfiable densities as controls.
problems.risk: The analytic bridge, Poisson/fixed-count and repeated/distinct-variable transfer, and series/error signs are load-bearing. A negative functional alone is only conditional evidence. No Lean validation of the cited preprint has been performed; do not claim a kernel-checked theorem. Success confidence is speculative.
review_requirements: Use three claim levels: floating-point negativity is evidence only; exact or interval negativity with rigorously signed truncation is a certified inequality only; a threshold theorem requires every analytic bridge to be written and accepted.

Threshold target: for each k in {4,5}, exhibit rational a_k below 10.23 and 21.33 respectively and prove P[F_k(n, floor(a_k n)) is satisfiable]->0 with independent clauses, uniformly chosen distinct variables within each clause, and independent fair signs.

Prove the general-k interpolation inequality for each selected k, explicitly checking odd k=5 hypotheses; finite-y or y-limit control; expectation-to-high-probability concentration; and Poisson/fixed-count plus repeated/distinct-variable transfers with explicit losses. Numerical replay cannot discharge these obligations. Vorobyev k=3 work is only a method lead.
Before using improves, recover the original source and random model behind the 10.23 and 21.33 baselines. Check Achlioptas-Menchaca-Mendez 2012 and its citing works for existing k>=4 numbers.
Tripwire: a value at or below cavity estimates 9.931 (k=4) or 21.117 (k=5) is a probable bug. Certify comfortable margins first (around k=4 at 9.96; k=5 at or above 21.14), not k=5 at 21.125.
Decide by about two attack hours whether the interpolation inequality holds; build certificate tools in parallel. Success confidence is speculative; 9.94 and 21.125 are search targets only.

Without all analytic bridges, report only a certified negative trial-functional value conditional on the stated inequality. Even with them, this is partial progress on Challenge 5: no lower bounds, no exact thresholds, and no solution of the broader program.
problems.solved_means: For k=4 and k=5, rational a_k below 10.23 and 21.33 with complete proofs that random k-SAT (independent clauses, distinct uniformly chosen variables, independent fair signs) with floor(a_k n) clauses is unsatisfiable with probability tending to one.
problems.partial_means: An exactly scoped verified result: a fully proved bound for one k, or a certified trial-functional inequality explicitly conditional on stated unproved analytic bridges.

review_overrides: This manifest and parent restrictions override stronger promises, confidence labels, and schedules in the screening catalogs.
The 14,400-second attack is part of each 21,600-second visit, not an extra allowance. Early termination and inconclusive outcomes are valid; no refill is implied.
Reserve new best, improved, or novel wording for the visit literature and novelty assessments; reproduction and restricted results keep their exact scope.

The replay sandbox forbids executing binaries created inside the attack directory. Every claims.json verify/check/control command must run with python3 or preinstalled system tools; preserve compiled-production logs as evidence instead.
